question: What is the primary purpose of communication in community health nursing?

options.C: Enforcing strict rules in the neighborhood clinic
options.D: Building trust and delivering health education

explanation: Community nurses use communication primarily to build relationships, gain trust, and teach people how to care for their health. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: Why is communication different in a community setting compared to a busy hospital ward?

options.A: Community nurses only use written notes instead of talking
options.B: Hospital patients never need verbal health instructions
options.C: Hospital care relies entirely on non-verbal body signs
options.D: Community nurses build long-term relationships with families

explanation: Because community nurses work closely with the same neighborhoods and families over time, their communication focuses heavily on long-term relationships and prevention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h1)

question: What part of the communication loop lets the nurse know if the client understood the message?
explanation: Feedback is the response given by the receiver, which tells the nurse whether the message was clearly understood. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: What happens when 'noise' or interference enters the communication process?

options.A: It speeds up how fast the sender talks to the receiver
options.B: It disrupts the message and can lead to misunderstandings
options.C: It changes the communication channel into a written format
options.D: It automatically guarantees the client will follow instructions

explanation: Noise represents any barrier or distraction that gets in the way of clear message transmission between sender and receiver. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h2)

question: Which of the following is an example of non-verbal communication?

options.A: Giving spoken instructions over the phone
options.B: Reading a printed pamphlet out loud
options.C: Using medical jargon during a lecture

explanation: Non-verbal communication involves physical cues like body language, posture, and facial expressions rather than spoken words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: A community nurse crosses their arms and looks at the floor while a client talks about their illness. What is the most likely effect of this behavior?

options.A: The client may feel ignored and stop sharing important details
options.B: The client will feel encouraged to ask more questions
options.C: The client will better understand their medication schedule
options.D: The client will appreciate the nurse saving time

explanation: Closed body language and lack of eye contact signal disinterest or judgment, which makes clients reluctant to open up. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h3)

question: What is the primary difference between hearing and active listening?

options.A: Active listening only happens during telephone conversations
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to take detailed written notes
options.C: Active listening requires full concentration and understanding
options.D: Hearing is a deliberate skill that takes years to learn

explanation: Hearing is just the physical detection of sound, whereas active listening is a conscious mental effort to comprehend the speaker's message and feelings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: Which statement best demonstrates empathy toward a client struggling with a new diagnosis?

options.A: You just need to follow your medication list every single day.
options.B: It must be really hard to adjust to these new lifestyle changes.
options.C: Why did you wait so long to see a doctor about your symptoms?
options.D: Everyone gets this disease eventually, so do not worry too much.

explanation: Acknowledging the client's emotional struggle shows empathy by validating their personal experience with the illness. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: Which of the following is NOT a barrier to effective communication?
explanation: Using simple and clear language helps communication succeed, whereas noise, pain, anxiety, and jargon act as barriers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: Why does severe anxiety or pain interfere with a client's ability to understand health instructions?

options.A: It limits the client's mental capacity to focus on new information
options.B: It forces the nurse to use complex medical terminology
options.C: It prevents the nurse from speaking in a normal tone of voice
options.D: It automatically makes the client deaf to any spoken sound

explanation: When a person is in intense pain or highly anxious, their brain is overwhelmed, making it very difficult to process and retain health teachings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h5)

question: What is cultural competence in nursing mainly about?

options.A: Convincing every client to abandon traditional home remedies
options.B: Speaking multiple foreign languages fluently before practicing
options.C: Treating every single patient using the exact same routine
options.D: Understanding and respecting diverse beliefs and health practices

explanation: Cultural competence involves recognizing and respecting cultural differences to provide safe, individualized nursing care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h6)

question: A community nurse is caring for a client who uses herbal remedies alongside prescribed medication. What is the best initial nursing action?

options.A: Ask open questions to understand the client's beliefs without judging
options.B: Ignore the herbal remedies because they do not affect western drugs
options.C: Tell the client immediately to throw away all their herbal remedies
options.D: Refuse to provide further care until the client stops home treatments

explanation: The best approach is to explore the client's practices respectfully and collaboratively, ensuring safe integration with medical treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h6)

question: What is a recommended strategy when communicating with an elderly client who has mild hearing loss?

options.A: Direct all your questions to their young family members
options.B: Write everything down and refuse to speak out loud
options.C: Shout at the top of your lungs from across the room
options.D: Speak clearly in a normal tone without shouting

explanation: Shouting distorts sound and can sound aggressive. Speaking clearly at a moderate pitch and facing the client works best for mild hearing loss. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: Why is the teach-back method especially useful when teaching clients with low health literacy?

options.A: It proves that the client has memorized complex medical terminology
options.B: It replaces the need for any non-verbal communication techniques
options.C: It confirms whether the client truly understood the instructions in their own words
options.D: It tests the nurse's ability to speak multiple foreign languages

explanation: Having clients repeat instructions in their own words ensures they grasp the care plan and catches any misunderstandings early. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h7)

question: What is the primary purpose of the teach-back method in health education?

options.A: To evaluate the environmental noise levels in a clinic room
options.B: To document medical history in a formal hospital chart
options.C: To check if the client understands the instructions by having them repeat them
options.D: To test the nurse's ability to lecture a large community group

explanation: Teach-back allows nurses to verify comprehension by asking clients to explain back what was taught in their own words. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)

question: Why is objective documentation of health education important for the community health team?

options.A: It guarantees that the client will follow their treatment plan perfectly
options.B: It replaces the need for face-to-face conversations with families
options.C: It prevents clients from ever asking follow-up questions
options.D: It ensures continuity of care so other nurses know what was taught

explanation: Clear notes allow different healthcare providers to see what education has already been provided, maintaining consistency in ongoing care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h8)
